newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ANDERSEN DOUBLE SINKS CELTIC IN OLD FIRM CLASH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ANDERSEN DOUBLE SINKS CELTIC IN OLD FIRM CLASH.

text.p: Two goals in the final seven minutes from substitute Eric Bo Andersen gave Glasgow Rangers a dramatic 3-1 victory over arch-rivals Celtic in the traditional New Year's "Old Firm" derby on Thursday.

Andersen, who came on midway through the second half at a time when Rangers were struggling to stem wave after wave of Celtic attacks, twice latched on to through-balls from German Joerg Albertz to beat goalkeeper Stewart Kerr on the break.

To rub salt into Celtic wounds, Portugal's Jorge Cadete, playing in his first Rangers-Celtic clash, had a goal disallowed in between Andersen's two strikes owing to what appeared to be a dubious decision by the linesman.
"Right now I'm in heaven," said Danish international Andersen, who had been rumoured to be on his way out of Ibrox after spending much of the season either injured or on the substitutes' bench.
"I'm going nowhere," Andersen promised when asked after the match about the rumours. "I'm still a Rangers player."
It was an eventful end to a game which had started brightly for Rangers when Albertz thundered home a free-kick from 30 metres after nine minutes.
The German blasted the ball at 78 mph (125 kmh) low into the left-hand side of Kerr's net, beating the keeper with sheer power.

The champions, seeking this season to equal Celtic's record by winning the Scottish title for the ninth time in a row, held on to their lead until halftime but were put under intense pressure after the break by the visitors, who needed a victory to keep their championship hopes alive.
The pressure finally resulted in an equaliser from Italian Paolo di Canio, who finished off a neat move involving Cadete and Dutch striker Pierre van Hooijdonk.
It was then that Andersen, who arrived at Ibrox from Danish side Aalborg for 1.5 million pounds ($2.5 million) came on and turned the match Rangers' way.
Victory leaves Rangers 14 points ahead of Celtic, who have two games in hand, and a massive 20 points ahead of Dundee United, Aberdeen and Hearts, who have all played a game more.
After the match, British bookmakers Ladbrokes closed their book on Rangers lifting their 47th Scottish title.
"Even though we're only two days into 1997 we've got no option but to stop betting," a spokesman said. "Nine consecutive League wins now looks a formality for Rangers..."
